section_summary: This section documents U.S. concern over Japan’s acquisition of petroleum, gasoline, metals, minerals, asbestos, abaca, and other strategic materials during spring 1941. It includes diplomatic and intelligence reporting, export-license data, studies of Philippine resources and Japan’s asbestos shortage, public protests, and correspondence about possible export restrictions. The closing pages concern congressional proposals to prohibit petroleum shipments to Japan and the State Department’s view that existing presidential export-control authority made such legislation unnecessary.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of information on Japanese petroleum purchases
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Walden’s report on information received from California concerning Japanese petroleum purchases.
subfiles.summary: Department thanks Walden for his April 21 letter on recent Japanese petroleum purchases.

subfiles.title: Persian Gulf oil exports to Japan
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Assesses the scale and controllability of Persian Gulf petroleum exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Persian Gulf oil was a small part of Japan's 1940 supply versus the United States; British papers explain the Anglo-Iranian contract; Britain could stop Gulf shipments if the US coordinated restrictions.

subfiles.title: Japanese purchases of Argentine copper and glycerine
subfiles.about: Reports offers of Argentine copper and sales of glycerine to Japanese buyers in Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Chandler says Argentine mines offer Japan copper at the New York price and Japan pays premiums for glycerine, vital for dynamite; urges investigation through the Buenos Aires embassy.

subfiles.title: Transmission of report on Argentine copper and glycerine
subfiles.about: Forwards Chandler’s confidential report and notes further inquiry into Argentine glycerine sales.
subfiles.summary: Finletter encloses the confidential letter on Argentine copper and glycerine from a reliable source; the Department seeks more from the Embassy.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Charles Lyon Chandler
subfiles.from: Frederick Livesey, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Thanks Chandler for reporting Japanese interest in Argentine copper and glycerine.
subfiles.summary: Livesey tells Chandler his information is of definite interest and thanks him.

subfiles.title: Metals Reserve offer for Mexican antimony
subfiles.about: Offers to buy Mexican antimony to prevent or replace contemplated shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Strauss says Metals Reserve will buy the Mexican antimony at fourteen cents a pound; duty difference on about 50,000 pounds monthly is the only obstacle; asks Finletter to relay the offer.

subfiles.title: Mexican antimony unavailable because of strike
subfiles.about: Reports that a mining strike has temporarily eliminated the company’s antimony surplus.
subfiles.summary: Finletter tells Strauss the Refining Company has no antimony because of a mine strike; Brownell will report when production resumes.

subfiles.title: Request for notice when Mexican antimony production resumes
subfiles.about: Asks Brownell to confirm the strike-related shortage and report any future exportable antimony surplus.
subfiles.summary: Finletter says he told Metals Reserve no Mexican antimony is available due to a strike, and asks for notice when an exportable surplus returns.

subfiles.title: German war matériel imported through the Trans-Siberian Railway
subfiles.from: H. S. Chase, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports German trucks, aircraft, engines, boats, drills, and other matériel entering Manchuria by rail.
subfiles.summary: Chase lists German equipment reportedly imported into Manchuria during February 1941, including combat aircraft, Jumo engines, motor torpedo boats, tractors, and industrial equipment. The British consul asks that British military and naval attachés in Tokyo not be told of the disclosure unless they independently provide the same information.

subfiles.title: Japanese vessels carrying Chilean minerals and metals
subfiles.about: Lists copper, wolfram, lead, and other ores exported from Antofagasta in Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Naval report on February 1941 cargoes carried from Antofagasta by Japanese vessels: copper, wolfram and lead ores, some of Bolivian origin.

subfiles.title: Protest against United States oil sales to Japan
subfiles.about: Demands an immediate halt to oil and other war-material exports to Japan and the Axis.
subfiles.summary: Hassan condemns continued American oil exports to Japan despite proclamations, enclosing New York Post clippings; he argues they undermine defense spending and arm potential enemies.

subfiles.title: San Diego League appeal to restrict steel and fuel oil exports
subfiles.from: Louise Darby, San Diego League for the Defense of Democracy
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt; copy to Cordell Hull
subfiles.about: Urges severe restriction of steel and fuel-oil exports to Japan and encloses a brochure describing the League.
subfiles.summary: Darby argues that Americans cannot understand supplying a potential foe and an enemy of China, while acknowledging the administration’s broader foreign-policy responsibilities. The enclosed brochure describes the League’s history, officers, speakers, committees, civil-rights work, and earlier protests against shipping war materials to Japan.

subfiles.title: Machine-tool shipment from Japan to India
subfiles.about: Reports that a single machine-tool consignment went from Japan to Alfred Herbert, Ltd. in Calcutta before further exports were prohibited.
subfiles.summary: Source R. H. Smith says only one machine-tool shipment went from Japan to India, allowed so Alfred Herbert, Ltd. could recover blocked credits; further shipments were prohibited.

subfiles.title: Petroleum shipments on Japanese naval tankers
subfiles.about: Provides Customs data on petroleum loaded at Pacific Coast ports by Japanese naval tankers.
subfiles.summary: Gaston reports no such shipments from the Los Angeles district since January 1 but notes that another Japanese vessel was expected. The attachment lists San Francisco-area shipments of gasoline, crude oil, and fuel oil by vessel, date, license, destination, quantity, and bunkers.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Japanese tanker shipment data
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Treasury data on petroleum shipments from San Francisco in Japanese naval tankers.
subfiles.summary: Acheson thanks Treasury for Gaston's letter and memorandum listing petroleum shipments from San Francisco on Japanese naval tankers.

subfiles.title: Availability of Philippine strategic materials for export
subfiles.about: Surveys Philippine iron, chrome, manganese, copper, abaca, copra, and coconut-oil production and exports.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum quantifies Philippine reserves, production, stocks, and shipments of iron ore, chrome, manganese, copper, abaca, copra, and coconut oil. It evaluates the Philippines’ importance to Japanese supply, especially after the reduction of American scrap-iron exports. It also records expanding Japanese and Russian purchases of abaca and coconut products, some believed destined ultimately for Germany.

subfiles.title: Internal note on cobalt procurement
subfiles.about: Urges prompt attention to acquiring cobalt for a United States stockpile.
subfiles.summary: Finletter says Clayton and Strauss stressed placing cobalt on the government's own supply line; asks Trueblood to pursue it.

subfiles.title: Correspondence urging control and stockpiling of cobalt
subfiles.from: S. D. Strauss, with enclosed letter from a deputy administrator
subfiles.to: Department of State and Office of Production Management
subfiles.about: Advocates treating cobalt as strategic and stopping leakage of supplies to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Strauss forwards material concerning cobalt, including an April 1 letter to the Office of Production Management. The enclosure notes dependence on the Belgian Congo, Northern Rhodesia, and Canada and argues that limited Axis-accessible supplies make cobalt stockpiling and export control desirable.

subfiles.title: Japan’s stocks and sources of crude asbestos
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy Tokyo
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japan’s severe asbestos shortage, import controls, foreign suppliers, and asbestos manufacturing industry.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy reports that Japan depended overwhelmingly on Canada, other British areas, and the United States for crude asbestos and had stocks sufficient for only two or three months. It describes government control of import quotas and distribution, military seizure of long-fiber supplies, Canadian export restrictions, and recent Japanese purchases in the American market. Seven tables trace imports, suppliers, American exports, Japanese production, employment, and export destinations from 1912 through 1940.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Tokyo asbestos despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards the Embassy’s confidential report on Japan’s crude-asbestos situation.
subfiles.summary: Moseley transmits the Embassy's confidential April 16 Tokyo despatch on crude asbestos in Japan.

subfiles.title: Gasoline licenses granted for export to Japan
subfiles.about: Reviews licenses for 42.75 million gallons of gasoline, much of it expressly intended for Japanese government or naval use.
subfiles.summary: Brewster argues that the quantities licensed during a ten-day period were excessive and calculates their potential aviation use in airplane-miles. The attachment lists each license, applicant, supplier, gasoline specification, volume, and stated purpose, including use by the Imperial Japanese Navy and other governmental agencies.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Canadian denial of wheat and pulp export licenses
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch concerning Canada’s refusal to license wheat and pulp exports to North China.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Japanese Foreign Office note to the Canadian Legation saying denied wheat and pulp licenses were not for military use.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Canadian export permit requirements
subfiles.about: Refers the reader to a Canadian Legation note concerning required export permits.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Canadian note of April 26 on export permit requirements; only a fragmentary subject survives.

subfiles.title: U.S. weighing Japan oil embargo and Axis fund freeze
subfiles.about: Reports speculation that the United States might embargo petroleum exports to Japan and freeze foreign funds.
subfiles.summary: Clipping reads Hull's willingness to discuss petroleum shipments and asset freezing as a sign action against Japan may be near.

subfiles.title: Radio Bulletin No. 104
subfiles.from: Division of Current Information, Department of State
subfiles.about: Summarizes presidential and State Department press conferences and other defense, diplomatic, and economic news.
subfiles.summary: Radio Bulletin 104: Roosevelt urges round-the-clock use of machine tools; Roosevelt and Hull decline to announce new petroleum restrictions; also Axis asset freezing, aircraft for Britain and other news.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on a crude-oil cargo
subfiles.about: Refers to a memorandum containing information about a cargo of crude oil.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference on a crude-oil cargo; vessel and destination illegible; original memorandum filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on tungsten negotiations
subfiles.about: Refers to a despatch reporting the current status of tungsten negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: May 7 despatch from Jenkins in Bolivia on tungsten negotiations, filed in the defense-materials series.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on scrap iron and new steel exports to Japan
subfiles.about: Refers to an inquiry about action on shipments of scrap iron and new steel to Japan amid the China-Japan dispute.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: letter asking what is being done about scrap-iron and new-steel exports to Japan.

subfiles.title: Prospective petroleum shipments from Shanghai up the Yangtze
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese Army permission for limited oil shipments to Yangtze installations and possible pressure for aviation gasoline.
subfiles.summary: Parker quotes a Shanghai cable: limited oil stocks may again move up the Yangtze under Japanese Army permits; no aviation gasoline went to Shanghai in the past year; he will consult Hornbeck before committing supplies.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Yangtze petroleum information
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Parker’s report on petroleum shipments from Shanghai up the Yangtze River.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Parker for information on petroleum moving from Shanghai to Yangtze ports.

subfiles.title: Senator Bone transmits Fidelia Frye’s protest
subfiles.from: Homer T. Bone, enclosing a letter from Fidelia Frye
subfiles.about: Forwards a constituent’s protest against oil shipments to Japan and munitions sales to Russia.
subfiles.summary: Bone sends Hull Fidelia Frye’s request that continued oil exports to Japan be investigated. Frye argues that it is inconsistent to aid China while selling Japan fuel used against it and also warns that munitions sold to Russia might threaten the United States or Britain.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Senator Bone
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Bone’s transmittal of Fidelia Frye’s protest about oil exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department confirms receipt of Bone’s May 16 letter and its enclosure. It promises prompt attention to Frye’s communication.

subfiles.title: Transfer sheet for document 894.24/1403
subfiles.about: Records the transfer of document 894.24/1403 to the defense-materials file.
subfiles.summary: The page contains no substantive correspondence. It indicates that the associated document was refiled under decimal classification 811.20 Defense (M).

subfiles.title: Request for State Department views on H.R. 4824
subfiles.from: Schuyler Otis Bland, House Committee on Merchant Marine and Fisheries
subfiles.about: Requests the Department’s opinion on a bill barring clearance of ships carrying petroleum to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Bland sends H.R. 4824, barring clearance of petroleum-laden ships bound for Japan, and asks for four copies of the Department's views.

subfiles.title: Submission of proposed H.R. 4824 report to the Bureau of the Budget
subfiles.about: Requests confirmation that the proposed State Department response on H.R. 4824 accords with the President’s program.
subfiles.summary: Hull sends the Budget Bureau a proposed H.R. 4824 report under Circular 344, asking if it fits the President's program.

subfiles.title: Preliminary reply to Chairman Bland on H.R. 4824
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of H.R. 4824 and promises a considered departmental report.
subfiles.summary: Hull tells Chairman Bland the Department is reviewing H.R. 4824 and will report fully later.

subfiles.title: Presidential approval note for the H.R. 4824 response
subfiles.doc_type: internal routing note and cover sheet
subfiles.from: Office of the Under Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Records President Roosevelt’s approval of the proposed letter opposing H.R. 4824.
subfiles.summary: The Under Secretary’s office informs Gray that the President approved the letter that morning. The following page is a Secretary of State letterhead cover associated with the approved response.

subfiles.title: Final State Department report opposing H.R. 4824
subfiles.about: Opposes H.R. 4824 because existing law already authorizes the President to restrict petroleum exports.
subfiles.summary: Hull opposes H.R. 4824 on foreign-policy grounds, noting section 6 of Public Law 703 already gives the President full power over exports, so denying ship clearance is unnecessary and undesirable.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of the H.R. 4824 report
subfiles.about: Preserves a duplicate of Hull’s letter opposing the petroleum-clearance bill.
subfiles.summary: The copy repeats the Department’s foreign-policy objection to H.R. 4824. It again argues that existing presidential authority is sufficient to restrict or prohibit petroleum exports and that refusing vessel clearance is an unnecessary device.

subfiles.title: Senator Brown forwards Jack J. Laade’s letter
subfiles.about: Forwards a Flint constituent’s letter and requests information for a reply.
subfiles.summary: Senator Brown forwards Jack Laade's letter from Flint, Michigan, asking for information to answer him and return of the enclosure.
